$schema_note: Machine-readable C# code quality rules, consumed by scripts/code_rule_checker.py. Each rule's 'source' says whether it was reverse-engineered from actual patterns in this codebase ('observed') or is a generic C# best practice applied because the codebase is silent on it ('best_practice'). Never blend the two silently — a reader must be able to tell this project's real contract from filler. Run the code-convention-miner agent against the target codebase to refill 'evidence' and to add project-specific rules.
generated_from: TEMPLATE — not yet mined from any codebase. Run code-convention-miner and replace this string with the sampled paths.

vendor_detection._note: How to recognise third-party code living inside the tree. Vendor code must never be linted — mixing it in produces false violations and erodes trust in the whole report. 'type_prefix' is the strongest signal when the project prefixes its own types (e.g. every first-party class starts with 'FG' / 'Acme'); leave it null if it doesn't, and rely on paths alone.

unit_discovery._note: How the checker splits the codebase into reportable units. 'directories_with_matching_manifest': a unit is any directory holding a file named after itself (foo/foo.json) — the convention in manifest-per-module codebases. 'top_level_directories': each immediate child of root is a unit. 'single_unit': the whole tree is one unit.

rules.description: Indentation is 4 spaces. No tabs.
Opening braces for types, methods, and control-flow blocks go on their own line (Allman style). Never '){' or '} else {' on one line. Single-statement expression bodies using '=>' are exempt.

check.note: character class deliberately excludes \n — with \s this would match legitimate Allman code where ')' ends one line and '{' begins the next

rules.description: Soft cap per line, plus a hard cap well above it. A line beyond the hard cap is almost always a bug (an accidentally minified or collapsed file), not a style choice. Set warn_over from the observed max across clean first-party files rather than from a habit.
Soft cap of 400 lines per file; hard cap of 600. A file between the two should be justified, not routine.

Exactly one public top-level type per file, and the filename matches the type name exactly (Foo.cs -> class Foo). A nested 'Builder' class living alongside its outer class is exempt — splitting the standard C# Builder-pattern nested type into its own file separates two things that are conceptually one unit.

Namespace segments mirror the folder path under the source root. Set 'root' to the source root and 'namespace_root' to the top-level namespace; a file at <root>/A/B/thing/*.cs must then declare a namespace at or under '<namespace_root>.A.B'.

First-party classes/structs are PascalCase and carry the project's own type prefix. Enable this ONLY if the project genuinely has such a prefix, and set the pattern accordingly (e.g. '^AC[A-Z]' for an 'AC' prefix). A nested 'Builder' class is exempt — it is already qualified by its outer class, so prefixing it again is stutter.

Interfaces are PascalCase prefixed with 'I' (IReceiptValidator, IAdProvider). List any legacy interface that predates the convention under known_exceptions rather than renaming it — and say in the description that it is not precedent for new ones.
Enums are PascalCase.

Private (and private-readonly) instance fields are prefixed with a leading underscore, then camelCase: _callbacks, _isInitialized. A private static field whose name already fully matches the constant pattern is exempt — a config-like pseudo-constant declared without the 'const'/'readonly' keyword is the same idiom as the constant rule's exceptions, not a casing mistake.

const fields (public or private) are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. If the project has a large, internally-consistent secondary convention in one subsystem (measured, not assumed), add it to exempt_name_patterns with the count as evidence rather than force-renaming it.

Public/protected properties and methods use PascalCase (standard .NET convention). Some names are dictated from outside the codebase and must NOT be renamed: interface members whose name the framework fixes, and members invoked by name across a native bridge (JNI/Objective-C), which break silently at runtime rather than at compile time. List those under known_exceptions with the reason. A member whose name already fully matches the constant pattern is also exempt: C# has no 'abstract const', so base classes commonly fake one with a read-only property named like a constant.

Local variables and method parameters use camelCase. Declared here for the record but not automated: locals and parameters cannot be extracted reliably with a line-oriented regex, and a checker that tries produces constant false positives.
Generic type parameters on base classes are single uppercase letters, and each is explained in an XML <typeparam> doc comment on the class.

Route logging through the project's own Log/LogWarning/LogError wrappers, not the platform's logger directly, so formatting and log-level policy live in one place. Set 'pattern' to the platform's raw logger (Unity: '\\bDebug\\.Log(Warning|Error)?\\s*\\(' — plain .NET: '\\bConsole\\.(Write|WriteLine)\\s*\\(') and exempt the units that implement the wrapper itself.
Do not leave commented-out lines of executable code in place; delete it (git history preserves it).
Never swallow an exception silently. Every catch block must at minimum log via the project's LogError/LogCritical wrapper.

Expose state via properties ('=>' expression-bodied where read-only), not public fields. Exempt: 'event' fields (C# events already restrict external access to +=/-=, which is not the uncontrolled-mutation problem this targets) and standalone 'readonly' fields (immutable after construction). In Unity, Inspector-exposed *Settings/ScriptableObject classes idiomatically use public fields — exempt them via exempt_type_suffix rather than annotating each one.

Every unit directory must contain its manifest file (id/settings discovered by convention, not hardcoded). Enable only in a codebase that actually has a per-unit manifest, and set 'pattern' to its glob.

Each unit's public API must live only on its designated facade class. Manager/Settings/Callbacks/Abstract classes exist to support it but should not themselves be the integration surface exposed to consumers. Enable only in a codebase that has this facade convention.

check.heuristic: flag public members on non-facade classes (Manager/Settings/Callbacks/Abstract suffix) that duplicate functionality already exposed on the facade

rules.description: Never modify vendored third-party files in place (see 'scope.vendor_detection'). If a bug looks like it's in vendor code, add or fix the wrapper around it instead. Not automatable from a snapshot — it needs the diff.

check.applies_to: git diff against excluded vendor paths
